argument_summary: The admissible record supports certification only in a narrow, caveated sense. Aggregate launch readiness passed by 2.2 percentage points and launch rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents, which supports a readiness finding. Public risk-management and model-card guidance also support deployment with measurement, monitoring, and documented limitations rather than requiring elimination of every issue before launch. But the same record does not cleanly support omission of a material-weakness disclosure because the enterprise refund workflow segment misses target by 1.8 percentage points, is named in a renewal success plan, legal review remains open, and the release policy ties disclosure to named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance. The appropriate treatment is therefore certification with an explicit caveat, not escalation based on a claim that the whole certification decision is unsupported.
claims_about_policy: The policy cuts against any broad claim of clean compliance on disclosure. Product characterizations such as non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality where the affected segment is tied to customer commitments or a named launch use case, and the policy note says such limitations must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. At the same time, the admissible evidence still supports a narrower compliance position on launch readiness itself because aggregate readiness passed and no severity-one rehearsal failures were recorded.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost argument is needed to justify the requested treatment. The position rests on the admissible governance and performance evidence, not on launch-velocity pressure.
concessions: The current record does not fully support omission of a material-weakness disclosure.
The named-segment gap and open legal review make a clean no-disclosure position weak.
The strongest defensible position is limited to launch readiness with documented limitations and monitoring, not full vindication of the disclosure choice.
